source_text: Λέγει ὁ Ναόδωρος τῷ Ὠριγένει· Ἡ ὁδὸς ἡμῶν οὐ κενὴ ἐγενήθη. Ὁ γὰρ ζητούμενος ηὑρέθη. Οὗτος ὑπὲρ τῶν Χριστιανῶν πάντων ἀπολογήσασθαι ἔχει. Καὶ προσαγαγόντων αὐτὸν τῷ ἡγεμόνι Ναόδωρος λέγει· Εὐμενείᾳ τῶν θεῶν καὶ προστάγματι τοῦ αὐτοκράτορος καὶ τῇ σῇ εὐτυχίᾳ, ἄρχον ἡμῶν ἐπίλεκτε, ηὑρέθη ὁ ζητούμενος φίλτατος τοῖς θεοῖς πᾶσιν πειθόμενος καὶ τοῖς νόμοις καὶ τῷ μεγάλῳ βασιλεῖ. Καὶ ὁ ἅγιος Κόνων μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ ἔφη· Οὐχ ὡς ἔστιν λέγεις· ἐγὼ γὰρ πείθομαι τῷ μεγάλῳ βασιλεῖ Χριστῷ. Ὠριγένης λέγει· Ἐπίλεκτε τῶν ἡγεμόνων, πολλὰ περιοδεύσαντες κύκλῳ τὰ περὶ τὴν πόλιν οὐδένα εὑρεῖν δεδυνήμεθα εἰ μὴ τὸν γέροντα τοῦτον ἐν κήπῳ τινί.
pass_a_gloss: Naodorus says to Origen: our way did not become empty; for the one sought was found; this one has to make defense on behalf of all Christians. And when they brought him to the governor, Naodorus says: by goodwill of the gods and by order of the emperor and by your fortune, our select ruler, the one sought was found, most dear, obeying all the gods and the laws and the great king. And holy Conon said with a great voice: you do not speak as it is; for I obey the great king Christ. Origen says: select of rulers, having gone about much in a circle through the things around the city we were able to find no one except this old man in a certain garden.
pass_b_english: Naodorus says to Origen, "Our journey has not proved fruitless, for the man we sought has been found. This fellow will have to answer on behalf of all the Christians." And when they brought him before the governor, Naodorus says, "By the kindness of the gods and by the emperor's command and by your good fortune, our excellent ruler, the man we sought has been found, a dear friend obedient to all the gods and to the laws and to the great king."

And Saint Conon cried out with a loud voice, "What you say is not as things are, for I obey the great King, Christ." Origen says, "Choice among rulers, after going about at length in a circuit through the districts around the city we were able to find no one except this old man in a certain garden."

choices.term: Ἡ ὁδὸς ἡμῶν οὐ κενὴ ἐγενήθη
choices.english: Our journey has not proved empty
choices.why: ὁδὸς here is the search expedition, not a road, and οὐ κενὴ with ἐγενήθη expresses result, not origin
rejected: Our road was not made empty

choices.why: dative after πείθομαι marks the obeyed authority, and Χριστῷ is in apposition correcting Naodorus's imperial great king
rejected: the great king Christ as emperor

choices.why: vocative singular ἐπίλεκτε with partitive genitive is a formal address to the governor, parallel to ἄρχον ἡμῶν ἐπίλεκτε
rejected: having been chosen by the rulers
